an1.219:1.1: Ānanda’s going-forth with other Sakyans is recounted at [pli-tv-kd17:1.4.1](). He played a key role in memorizing discourses ([dn18:29.3]()), and led the discourse recitation at the First Council ([pli-tv-kd21:1.2.4]()). He survived the Buddha, and his verses are at [thag17.3](). | “Very learned” is literally “heard much”, since it was an oral tradition. This set of four qualities all highlight key skills needed for accurate oral transmission.
an1.220:1.1: “Memory” is _sati_ in its old meaning, the capacity to recall what was said and done long ago ([sn48.9:3.2]()). | These three terms are found together in this sense at [mn12:62.6](), which indicates their meaning. [dn28:12.2]() adds “eloquence” and “thoughtfulness”.
an1.221:1.1: The exact sense of _gati_ (“motion”) here is obscure. At Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.4.4 it means something like the “course of meaning” or the “unfolding of sense”. The commentary says it means “proficiency in binding what is retained”. Perhaps it has to do with the sequence of texts; noting the pattern of tropes and keywords is important to memorization. [mn12:62.9]() speaks of how experts will remember the answers and not ask the same question twice.
an1.224:1.1: He was the senior of three Kassapa brothers, leading a community of 500 Brahmanical students before converting to Buddhism [pli-tv-kd1:15.1.3](). Apart from his verses at [thag6.1](), he does not appear in the Suttas, and is only mentioned in passing in one other Vinaya context ([pli-tv-kd15:37.1.1]()).
an1.225:1.1: His verses at [thag10.1]() praise the Buddha’s family.
an1.226:1.1: Famed for his severer ascetic practices at [mn124]()—which also mentions his good health—his few Theragāthā verses are simple and lack the severity of the prose ([thag3.3]()).
an1.227:1.1: He claims to have recollected 500 eons in a single night ([thag2.23]()), a claim doubted by some but affirmed by the Buddha ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pj4:9.7.1]()).
an1.228:1.1: There are several Upālis in the Pali canon, but this is the Sakyan who went forth along with Ānanda and Anuruddha. He features occasionally in the Suttas (eg. [an10.31]()), but in the Vinaya he frequently engages in detailed discussions on fine points of monastic law, on which his expertise was praised by the Buddha ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pc72:1.2]()). He regarded Vinaya as the foundation for the spiritual life ([thag3.11]()).
an1.229:1.1: Nandaka was praised for his teaching of monks ([an9.4]()). At [an3.66]() he taught the layman Sāḷha how to discern the true teaching. His fame in advising nuns stems from [mn146](). There are two Nandakas in the Theragāthā; according to the commentary, his are the four verses at [thag4.4](). A second Nandaka at [thag2.27]() was the brother of Bharata ([thag2.28]()).
an1.230:1.1: Nanda was the Buddha’s cousin, said to be only two inches shorter than him ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pc92:1.2]()). His practice of sense restraint is praised at [an8.9](). His efforts in this regard were prompted by the famous episode at [ud3.2](), where his desire to disrobe was dispelled with the promise of heavenly nymphs. His former sensual nature is seen at [sn21.8]().
an1.231:1.1: One of the great disciples, he is described as “white, thin, with a pointy nose” ([sn21.11]()). Two of his enlightened students appear in [sn21.12]() as testament to his skill in advising monks. He is seen meditating at [sn54.7](), and his verses are at [thag10.3]().
an1.232:1.1: Sāgata was once the Buddha’s attendent, and, unusually, the Buddha asked him to make a demonstration of psychic powers for householders ([pli-tv-kd5:1.7.4]()). At [pli-tv-bu-vb-pc51:1.1]() he is able to master a fire-breathing dragon, but himself is mastered by drink. He must have recovered from that disgrace to be praised here.
an1.233:1.1: Rādha questions the Buddha on countless occasions, making up a whole Saṁyutta (SN 23). His verses are at [thag2.7]().
an1.234:1.1: Best known for his verses in the Way to the Far Shore ([snp5.16]()), Mogharāja also features in [thag2.44](), where he lives outdoors, and [sn1.34:7.2.](), where he appears abruptly to ask a question.
